title: PowerShell compatibility profile
description: Declares which PowerShell version's OBSERVABLE SEMANTICS a BrowserShell session emulates. A profile is data, never code: the engine reads it at boot and the same command implementation behaves differently under different profiles. Adding a version must never mean forking a command.

displayVersion.description: What the session banner and $PSVersionTable report. Must equal source.releaseTag minus its leading v, or be explicitly justified in notes.

inherits.description: Profile id this one is a delta against. Resolution order is parent-first, so a derived profile overrides what it inherits. `behaviors` and `documentedBehaviors` REPLACE per key: they are flat scalars and there is nothing inside one to merge. `commands` DEEP-MERGES per command: a child that sets only `notes` on an inherited command keeps that command's `availability`, and `parameterPatches` merge per parameter. Removal is expressed as data (`availability: "removed"` with `removedIn`), never as absence, so deep-merging cannot hide a deletion. Cycles are a hard error.

source.description: Provenance. Every field here is copied from the release-truth lockfile, never typed by hand.

derivedFrom.description: Which lockfile generation produced this profile.

bundledModules.description: Modules shipped in the box at this version, as stated by the release notes.

behaviors.description: The semantic switchboard THE ENGINE READS. Every entry is a behaviour a command implementation may branch on, and every entry is one BrowserShell actually emulates and proves with a test. A documented-but-unemulated difference belongs in `documentedBehaviors`; putting it here would serve a claim we cannot support as live execution semantics. Keys are command- and parameter-scoped, dotted, stable and documented; a key is added here BEFORE any command reads it.

behaviorDocs.description: Human explanation plus upstream citation for each behavior key. A behavior without a doc entry fails validation in CI: an undocumented flag is a guess.

documentedBehaviors.description: EVERY documented upstream difference, whether or not BrowserShell emulates it. This is the honest half of the compatibility record and it is deliberately NOT the table the engine reads: `behaviors` holds only what we reproduce, and a key appears there only when `emulated` is true here. Keeping them apart is the fix for a defect in which the generator wrote every documented-but-unemulated change into the runtime profile, so commands were served thirteen behaviour flags the engine did not implement. Nothing under src/ may read this.

value.description: The value for THIS profile's version.

baselineValue.description: What the older PowerShell does, derived from upstreamValue.

implementation.description: What BrowserShell does about it. Only implemented/verified may reach `behaviors`.

emulated.description: True exactly when a command can read this key from `behaviors`.

scope.description: Where the behaviour applies. `command: null` is an explicit claim that the upstream change really is engine-wide.

commands.description: Per-command availability and metadata patches, applied over the base command manifest. Absent command means inherit from parent profile.

engineLimits.description: Where BrowserShell knowingly diverges from upstream. Stating a limit is mandatory; silently behaving differently is not allowed.
